description: Minnesota-only rules checked against Minnesota Statutes. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Where no special hazard exists, Minnesota's speed for an urban district is 30 mph. A speed over a listed limit is prima facie unlawful, except that
options: Every listed limit is only prima facie, including inside a municipality
Inside any municipality the limit is a maximum, and any excess is unlawful
Urban districts are 25 mph if the street has a sidewalk
30 mph applies only when a sign repeats it
questions.explanation: Minn. Stat. §169.14, subd. 2(a), makes speeds over the listed limits prima facie evidence that the speed is not reasonable or prudent and that it is unlawful, except that the speed limit within any municipality is a maximum limit. The urban-district figure in clause (1) is 30 mph.

questions.q: On interstate highways outside an urbanized area with a population greater than 50,000, the listed speed is
questions.explanation: Section 169.14, subd. 2(a)(4), lists 70 mph on interstate highways outside an urbanized area with a population greater than 50,000, as defined by order of the commissioner of transportation. Inside such an urbanized area, clause (5) lists 65 mph on interstate highways.

questions.q: In locations other than the urban, expressway, freeway, interstate, alley, and adopted residential speeds named in the subdivision, the listed speed is
questions.explanation: Section 169.14, subd. 2(a)(3), lists 55 mph in locations other than those specified in the section. Noninterstate expressways and noninterstate freeways are listed separately at 65.

questions.q: A local school speed limit may not be lower than 15 mph and may not be more than 30 mph below the established limit. It is effective
options: Whenever a school building is within a half mile, even with no sign
When signs mark the speed and the zone's beginning and end
Only if a crossing guard is present
questions.explanation: Section 169.14, subd. 5a, sets those limits and says the school speed limit is effective upon erection of appropriate signs designating the speed and indicating the beginning and end of the reduced speed zone. It applies when children are present, going to or leaving school during opening or closing hours, or during school recess periods.

questions.q: Minnesota's driving-while-impaired crime includes an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more
options: When driving, or as measured within two hours
Only if a blood sample is taken at the scene
questions.explanation: Minn. Stat. §169A.20, subd. 1(5), uses 0.08 or more at the time, or as measured within two hours of the time, of driving, operating, or being in physical control.

questions.q: If the vehicle is a commercial motor vehicle, the impaired-driving alcohol concentration is
options: 0.08 or more, with no separate commercial figure
0.04 or more at the time, or as measured within two hours
questions.explanation: Section 169A.20, subd. 1(6), uses 0.04 or more for a commercial motor vehicle, at the time or as measured within two hours of driving, operating, or being in physical control.

questions.q: Minnesota's under-21 offense is driving, operating, or being in physical control
options: At 0.02 or more but less than 0.08
questions.explanation: Minn. Stat. §169A.33, subd. 2, states that crime. It does not use a 0.02 concentration. If the conduct also violates section 169A.20, subdivision 5 says those impaired-driving sanctions apply instead of the under-21 license sanction. While consuming alcoholic beverages, or after consuming them while physical evidence of the consumption is present in the body.

questions.q: Minnesota's speed statute does not use a demerit-point total. The driver's license of a person who violates a speed limit in section 169.14 by driving in excess of 100 mph is revoked for
questions.explanation: Section 169.14 states that six-month revocation under section 171.17, or a longer minimum under section 169A.53, 169A.54, or 171.174. The revisor pages opened for this file do not publish a point schedule.

questions.q: A first finding of the under-21 drinking-and-driving offense results in a license or operating-privilege suspension of
options: 30 days, or 180 days for a repeat
Six months for every first offense
questions.explanation: Section 169A.33, subd. 4, requires the commissioner to suspend for 30 days, or for 180 days if the person was previously found to have violated that subdivision or a conforming statute or ordinance.

questions.q: An instruction permit for a person age 15, 16, or 17 requires the permit holder to be accompanied and supervised by a certified driver-education instructor, the parent or guardian, or another licensed driver age 21 or older who
options: May supervise from the back seat
Occupies the seat beside the permit holder
Is related to the permit holder
Has held a license for five years
questions.explanation: Section 171.05, subd. 2b, requires the permit in possession and that supervisor in the seat beside the permit holder. Subdivision 2a requires the permit to be held at least six months before a driver's license.

questions.q: A provisional license may be issued at 16. The supervised-driving log must show at least 40 hours, at least 15 of them at night, with a licensed driver at least 21, and the applicant must also have either
options: 10 more hours, or a parent-curriculum certificate
No further hours if a school signs the form
questions.explanation: Section 171.055, subd. 1(a)(5) and (6), states the 40-hour log, the 15 nighttime hours, and the choice between 10 additional hours and the supplemental-parental-curriculum certification.

questions.q: For the first six months of a provisional license, the holder may not carry more than one passenger under 20 who is not an immediate-family member unless
options: A parent or guardian rides along
questions.explanation: Section 171.055, subd. 2(c), sets one such passenger for the first six months and not more than three for the second six months. The paragraph does not apply if a parent or guardian accompanies the holder.

questions.q: In Minnesota, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Minnesota issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Minnesota car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Minnesota, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Minnesota requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Minnesota complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Minnesota requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Graduated driver's license | Minnesota Department of Public Safety

questions.q: Of a Minnesota teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Minnesota requires at least 15 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Minnesota: 15 hours of the supervised driving at night.

questions.q: In Minnesota, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Minnesota, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Graduated driver's license - Minnesota Department of Public Safety

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Minnesota not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Minnesota restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Minnesota new drivers: off the road Midnight to 5 a.m..

provenance.manual: Teen driver laws | Minnesota Department of Public Safety

questions.q: In Minnesota, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Minnesota drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Minnesota car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Minnesota car knowledge test has 40 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Minnesota car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Minnesota car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Minnesota, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Minnesota, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Minnesota, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Minnesota, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Minnesota sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

provenance.manual: Teen driver laws | Minnesota Department of Public Safety

questions.q: In Minnesota, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Minnesota brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Minnesota, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Minnesota residential district?
questions.explanation: Minnesota sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Minnesota?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Minnesota can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Minnesota rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Minnesota's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Minnesota: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Minnesota?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Minnesota, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Minnesota left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Minnesota's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Minnesota seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: A simple click can save your life. Protect yourself and your loved ones by buckling up. | Minnesota Department of Public Safety

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Minnesota?
questions.explanation: Minnesota requires a car seat or booster until 9 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Minnesota: car or booster seat until 9 years.

questions.q: What is Minnesota's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Minnesota requires at least $30,000 / $60,000 / $10,000.
